description: Scorching Light is a 10-15 minute horror-action-puzzle platformer made as a real Game Boy game with GB Studio. Light enemies, glowing items, and luminous liquid are lethal, so the protagonist must blend into the environment, watch the hidden-status eye, and move through the nightmare without touching the light.
intro: The page targets the questions this compact game creates: what counts as light, how hiding works, how to find the obscured protagonist, the keyboard and controller mapping, and how to approach a short no-light route without losing track of the character.
guideTitle: Scorching Light Walkthrough, Hiding, and Controls Guide
guideIntro: Treat every bright object as a hazard until proven otherwise. Progress comes from reading safe dark space, blending into matching scenery, and using the eye indicator instead of relying only on the character sprite.
steps: Move and climb with WASD or the arrow keys, or use the directional pad on a Game Boy, Xbox, or PlayStation controller.
Avoid light enemies, glowing items, and luminous liquid because every source of light can kill the protagonist.
Blend into the environment when light enemies approach and check the eye at the bottom of the screen to confirm that you are hidden.
Press Shift on keyboard, Select on Game Boy, or View on Xbox to show a temporary character outline when the protagonist disappears into the scenery.
Jump with Z, J, or Space on keyboard, or the A button on Game Boy and Xbox, and plan the landing so it stays outside the next light zone.
